messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-ECOLOGY members

A reminder - Clarify ecological comparisons before translating field and monitoring data into estimates. Data Can Deceive: Causal Roadmaps is a seminar livestreaming August 5 with Robert Platt (School of Population and Global Health, McGill University), Kathryn Morrison (Precision Analytics), and Andy Wilson (Spencer Fox Eccles School of Medicine, University of Utah). Formulate causal estimands, map assumptions with directed acyclic graphs, and build target-trial protocols for observational ecological studies. Apply these tools to vegetation, soil, hydrology, or other environmental data in R by aligning eligibility, time zero, exposures, and outcomes. Evaluate confounding and inappropriate adjustment, then document analytic decisions so collaborators can audit the resulting causal claim.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/data-can-deceive-causal-roadmaps
Further information is available on the seminar page.


Best wishes

messages.subject: [R-sig-eco] Handle species occurrence data in R (live online course)
messages.subject_clean: Handle species occurrence data in R (live online course)
messages.body_plain:
Dear colleagues,

Transmitting Science is offering the course "Species occurrence data 
download and cleaning with R" (8th edition).

Course webpage: 
https://www.transmittingscience.com/courses/ecology/species-occurrence-data-download-and-cleaning-with-r

Species occurrence data are essential for a range of ecological and 
biogeographical analyses. Although they are now widely available in 
multiple online sources, they are heterogeneous and come with caveats 
that need to be addressed before moving on with the analysis.

In this short course, we will use a range of tools to:
*    Import species occurrence data from various sources into R (e.g. 
GBIF, iNaturalist, VertNet, EcoEngine)
*    Join and arrange these data into a homogeneous dataset for analysis
*    Map and visually inspect the data for taxonomic and spatial errors 
and bias
*    Clean the data by removing detectable errors
*    Correct or minimise spatial bias

The course will be highly interactive and will include both theoretical 
and practical sessions. Participants are encouraged to work with their 
own species of interest, although several illustrative examples will 
also be provided.

For any questions, please write to courses at transmittingscience.com
Best regards,

Haris

-- 
Haris Saslis, PhD
Course Coordinator
Transmitting Science

messages.subject: [R-sig-eco] PR stats live courses for 2026
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

Below is a list of our upcoming live courses covering ecology and related methods, including statistical, spatial, genomic, and computational approaches with strong applications to ecological research.

Please feel free to share this email with colleagues, friends, and others within your institute, organisation, or wider research network.
Ecology
Species Distribution Modelling With Bayesian Statistics (SDMB08)<https://prstats.org/course/species-distribution-modelling-with-bayesian-statistics-sdmb08/>
Model species distributions using BART in R. Covers uncertainty, variable selection, and full Bayesian workflow.

Joint Species Distribution Modelling (JSDM) using HMSC: A Hierarchical Modelling Approach (JSDM01)<https://prstats.org/course/joint-species-distribution-modelling-jsdm01/>
Analyse entire ecological communities with hierarchical models and joint species distribution modelling in R.

Bioacoustics Data Analysis (BIAC06)<https://prstats.org/course/bioacoustics-data-analysis-biac06/>
Analyse animal acoustic signals in R. Learn spectrograms, annotations, and bioacoustics workflows.

Path Analysis, Structural Equations, and Causal Inference for Biologists (PSCB04)<https://prstats.org/course/path-analysis-structural-equations-and-causal-inference-for-biologists-pscb04/>
Learn path analysis and structural equation modelling in R. Practical online training in causal inference and SEM workflows.

Analysing Ecological Data with Detection Error (AEDD02)<https://prstats.org/course/analysing-ecological-data-with-detection-error-aedd02/>
Learn to analyse ecological field data with detection error using R. Work with point counts, ARU data, N-mixture models, distance sampling and time-removal methods.

Multivariate Analysis of Ecological Communities Using VEGAN (VGNR10)<https://prstats.org/course/multivariate-analysis-of-ecological-communities-using-vegan-vgnr10/>
Analyse ecological community data in R using VEGAN. Learn ordination, clustering, and multivariate statistics with real datasets.

Network Analysis for Ecological Data (NWAE02)<https://prstats.org/course/network-analysis-for-ecological-data-nwae02/>
Use R to analyse ecological networks. Learn metrics, simulation, and visualisation with igraph.

Statistics

Bayesian Modelling Using R-INLA Course (BMIN04)<https://prstats.org/course/bayesian-modelling-using-r-inla-bmin04/>

Learn Bayesian modelling with the R-INLA package. Build, fit, and interpret INLA models, define priors and latent effects, and apply INLA to real data in a five day course.



Hierarchical Generalized Additive Models for Biological Sciences (HGAM01)<https://prstats.org/course/hierarchical-generalized-additive-models-for-biological-sciences-hgam01/>

Learn hierarchical generalized additive models (HGAMs) to analyse nonlinear, hierarchical, and grouped biological data using R.

Spatial / Mapping
Advanced Static Cartography (ASCR01)<https://prstats.org/course/advanced-static-cartography-ascr01/>
Turn spatial data into clear, publication-quality maps using advanced cartography in R.

Introduction to QGIS and Spatial Data Analysis Workflows (IQGI01)<https://prstats.org/course/introduction-to-qgis-and-spatial-data-analysis-workflows-iqgi01/>
Learn QGIS and spatial data analysis workflows. Practical online training in mapping, GIS, and spatial data processing.

Advanced QGIS and Spatial Data Analysis Workflows (AQGI01)<https://prstats.org/course/advanced-qgis-and-spatial-data-analysis-workflows-aqgi01/>
Learn QGIS and spatial data analysis workflows. Practical online training in mapping, GIS, and spatial data processing.

Reproducible Spatial Ecology: Visualization, Reporting, and AI-Assisted Workflows with R (RSPE02)<https://prstats.org/course/reproducible-spatial-ecology-visualization-reporting-and-ai-assisted-workflows-with-r-rspe02/>
Learn reproducible spatial ecology workflows in R. Practical online training in spatial analysis and ecological data workflows.

Introduction to Spatial Data analysis and GIS Workflows in R (IRGI01)<https://prstats.org/course/introduction-to-spatial-data-analysis-and-gis-workflows-in-r-irgi01/>
Learn spatial data analysis and GIS workflows in R. Practical online training in sf, tmap, mapping, and spatial data processing.

Advanced Spatial Analysis Workflows in R (ARGI01)<https://prstats.org/course/advanced-r-for-spatial-analysis-argi01/>
Learn advanced spatial analysis workflows in R using sf & tmap. Practical online training in vector and spatial modelling workflows.

Genetics
Spatial Phylogenetics and the Bayesian Phylogenetic Mixed Model (PMM) (BPMM01)<https://prstats.org/course/spatial-phylogenetics-and-the-bayesian-phylogenetic-mixed-model-pmm-bpmm01/>
Learn spatial phylogenetics and Bayesian phylogenetic mixed models in R. Practical online training in phylogenetic modelling and comparative workflows.

Bioinformatics / Genomics
Machine Learning for Evolutionary Genomics (MLEG01)<https://prstats.org/course/machine-learning-for-evolutionary-genomics-mleg01/>
Machine Learning for Evolutionary Genomics: learn predictive modelling, data analysis, and AI methods for genomic data.

RNA-Seq Analysis (RNAA02)<https://prstats.org/course/rna-seq-analysis-rnaa02/>
RNA-Seq analysis training ? live online course covering experiment design, data QC, alignment, gene expression, DESeq2 differential expression, PCA, visualisation, and functional analysis.

Genomic Prediction of Complex Traits (GPCT01)<https://prstats.org/course/genomic-prediction-of-complex-traits-gpct01/>
Genomic Prediction of Complex Traits: learn predictive modelling, polygenic prediction, and genomic methods for analysing complex traits.

Population Genomics and Structure Analysis (PGSA01)<https://prstats.org/course/population-genomics-and-structure-analysis-pgsa01/>
Learn population structure analysis for evolutionary biology using genetic data, population genetics methods, and evolutionary inference.

Deep Learning for Evolutionary Genomics (DLEG01)<https://prstats.org/course/deep-learning-for-evolutionary-genomics-dleg01/>
Deep Learning for Evolutionary Genomics: learn neural networks, predictive modelling, and AI methods for genomic data analysis.

Single cell RNA-Seq analysis (SCRN03)<https://prstats.org/course/single-cell-rna-seq-analysis-scrn03/>
Learn single cell RNA-Seq analysis with Seurat, 10x Genomics, and advanced QC methods. Gain cell type-specific insights in this live online course.

Ancient DNA Analysis (ADNA01)<https://prstats.org/course/ancient-dna-analysis-adna01/>
Ancient DNA Analysis: learn bioinformatics workflows, population genetics, and genomic analysis for ancient DNA research.

Metagenomic Data Analysis of Microbial Communities (MGMC01)<https://prstats.org/course/metagenomic-data-analysis-of-microbial-communities-mgmc01/>
Learn metagenomic data analysis for microbial communities. Analyse shotgun sequencing data, profile microbiomes, and interpret microbial diversity using R.

Genome-Wide Association Studies (GWAS) for Evolutionary Biology (GWAS01)<https://prstats.org/course/genome-wide-association-studies-gwas-for-evolutionary-biology-gwas01/>
GWAS for Evolutionary Biology: learn genome-wide association studies, quantitative trait analysis & genomic methods for evolutionary data.

Ancient Environmental Metagenomics (AEMG01)<https://prstats.org/course/ancient-environmental-metagenomics-aemg01/>
Ancient Environmental Metagenomics: learn bioinformatics workflows, taxonomic profiling, and genomic analysis of ancient environmental DNA.

Introduction to Snakemake (SNKM03)<https://prstats.org/course/introduction-to-snakemake-snkm03/>
Learn Snakemake to automate data workflows. Build reproducible, scalable pipelines for research with hands-on training in this 4-day live online course.

Genomics and Bioinformatics for Non-Model Organisms (BNMO01)<https://prstats.org/course/genomics-and-bioinformatics-for-non-model-organisms-bnmo01/>
Bioinformatics for Non-Model Organisms: learn genome assembly, annotation, and genomic analysis for non-model species.

Ancient Microbiome and Pathogen Genomics (AMPG01)<https://prstats.org/course/ancient-microbiome-and-pathogen-genomics-ampg01/>
Ancient Microbiome and Pathogen Genomics: learn bioinformatics, metagenomics, and genomic analysis of ancient microbial and pathogen DNA.


Thanks,

Oliver

oliver at prstats.org

messages.subject: [R-sig-eco] New open-access AI readiness toolkit for universities
messages.subject_clean: New open-access AI readiness toolkit for universities
messages.body_plain:
Hello?everyone

I'm sharing a new open-access resource that you may find useful: The Institutional AI Readiness Pack <https://instats.org/publications/the-institutional-ai-readiness-pack> and its accompanying instruments catalogue <https://mzyphur.github.io/ai-readiness/instruments.html>.?

Universities increasingly have AI policies, but many still lack an evidence-based picture of how AI is actually used and governed across their research environments. Without that picture, they cannot reliably identify gaps across policy, people, systems, and process, nor can they determine how to strengthen the institutional capabilities that enable rigorous and responsible AI use in research. That is the gap this pack closes.?

The pack accompanies Responsible AI in Academic Research: A Competency Framework for Research Training <https://instats.org/publications/responsible-ai-in-academic-research>, which defines five dimensions of institutional readiness and the capabilities that underpin them. It turns that framework into an institutional self-assessment, surveys for graduate students and supervisors, gap-analysis and action-planning tools, model policy and disclosure materials, agreements, and briefings for university leaders. Every instrument is openly licensed under CC BY 4.0 and available in HTML, Word, and PDF.?

The framework is non-prescriptive about which maturity level an institution should occupy. Nobody outside your university is grading the exercise. There is no prize for a high score and no penalty for a low one. The real risk is relying on an inaccurate picture.?

For researchers, graduate students, and universities that want more structured training on AI in academic research, Instats is running a four-part seminar series <https://instats.org/course/agentic-ai-for-academic-research1> this month and next on how to understand and use AI for academic research. It covers AI as a Research Method, Responsible AI for Academic Research, Verifiable AI for Academic Research, and Building Agentic AI Research Teams. Each seminar stands alone, but together they provide a coherent progression for developing the knowledge and skills needed to use AI effectively for rigorous and honest research.

I hope you find the pack useful, and I hope you can join us for the seminar series. Please feel free to share both with students and colleagues working in research leadership, training, integrity, policy, or graduate education.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur

messages.subject_clean: Online course: Applied Longitudinal Data Analysis
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-ECOLOGY members

Develop a clearer framework for studying environmental change across repeated observations. Applied Longitudinal Data Analysis led by Han Du (Department of Psychology, University of California, Los Angeles) is now available as an on-demand streaming seminar. Multilevel models, latent growth curves, and nonlinear change models can analyze repeated ecological and environmental measurements in R and SPSS. Researchers can use these approaches to examine change within sites or organisms while assessing differences across them. Model selection, mediation, and dyadic methods extend longitudinal analyses for vegetation, soils, hydrology, and related data.

Course details: https://instats.org/seminar/applied-longitudinal-data-analysis-1
The full course outline is available on the Instats course page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur

messages.subject: [R-sig-eco] Online course: Genomics Ecological Evolutionary Studies
messages.subject_clean: Online course: Genomics Ecological Evolutionary Studies
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-ECOLOGY members

Computational genomic evidence can extend ecological questions from populations to sequence variation. Genomics for Ecological and Evolutionary Studies led by Giulio Formenti (Vertebrate Genome Lab, The Rockefeller University) and Guido Gallo (Department of Biosciences, University of Milan) is now available as an on-demand streaming seminar. Sequencing-data processing, read alignment, variant calling, and genome assembly provide practical foundations for ecological and evolutionary genomic analysis. Ecologists using R can apply these workflows when preparing genomic evidence to investigate biodiversity, adaptation, and evolutionary history. Comparing short- and long-read alignments and evaluating assembly statistics supports informed interpretation of sequence-derived results.

Course details: https://instats.org/seminar/genomics-for-ecological-and-evolutionary-1
Further information is available on the Instats course page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director
